message.content:
The title “best jazz singer” is a matter of taste and context, but there are a handful of artists who are almost universally celebrated for their artistry, influence, and vocal mastery. Below are some of the most frequently cited names, along with a brief note on why they’re held in such high regard:

| Artist | Key Contributions & Why They’re Revered |
|--------|------------------------------------------|
| **Ella Fitzgerald** | Known as the “First Lady of Song,” Ella’s impeccable pitch, scat‑sing brilliance, and effortless phrasing set a gold standard for jazz vocalists. Her recordings with Duke Ellington, Count Basie, and her own “Songbooks” remain essential listening. |
| **Billie Holiday** | Billie’s deeply emotive delivery, unique phrasing, and ability to convey raw feeling made her a pioneer of vocal jazz. Her interpretations of standards like “God Bless the Child” and “Strange Fruit” are still considered definitive. |
| **Sarah Vaughan** | With a rich, contralto voice and a wide vocal range, Vaughan blended jazz, blues, and pop. Her technical control and improvisational skill earned her the nickname “The Divine One.” |
| **Nat King Cole** | Though often grouped with pop, Nat’s smooth baritone and sophisticated phrasing made him a key figure in early jazz vocalism. His hits “Unforgettable” and “Mona Lisa” showcase his timeless appeal. |
| **Cassandra Wilson** | A modern torch‑song specialist, Wilson’s powerful voice and emotional depth have earned her acclaim as one of the leading jazz singers of the 21st century. |
| **Diana Krall** | Combining jazz standards with contemporary pop, Krall’s husky voice and piano skills have made her a global superstar in the jazz world. |
| **Tony Parker** | A master of the “swing” style, Parker’s smooth tenor and impeccable timing have made him a staple in the jazz vocal canon. |
| **Nina Simone** | Known for her dramatic intensity and improvisational prowess, Simone’s blend of jazz, blues, and gospel set her apart as a powerful storyteller. |

### How to Choose the “Best”
- **Historical Impact** – If you’re looking at influence on the genre, Ella Fitzgerald and Billie Holiday often top the list.
- **Technical Mastery** – For vocal technique and range, Sarah Vaughan and Nina Simone are frequently highlighted.
- **Modern Relevance** – Cassandra Wilson and Diana Krall bring contemporary sensibilities while staying true to jazz roots.

Ultimately, the “best” singer will depend on what you value most—emotional expression, technical skill, historical significance, or modern innovation. Each of the artists above has left an indelible mark on jazz, and exploring their recordings is a great way to discover which style resonates most with you.
